01-序章中式书房: Quiet traditional Chinese study scene, unhurried pentatonic. Guqin plucked phrases answered by soft xiao bamboo flute, faint paper-turning and brush texture as gentle percussion, warm intimate close-mic feel, ink and old archive atmosphere, a sealed letter waiting to be opened. Slow tempo 58-66 BPM, five-tone scale, generous silence between phrases, no western instruments, no drums, instrumental only.
02-黄花阵中秋灯会: Bright Qing palace Mid-Autumn lantern night, playful but orderly. Dizi bamboo flute leads a skipping pentatonic melody, pipa and yangqin sparkle like lantern light, soft wooden clappers suggest people running through maze paths, moonlight and distant laughter. Medium-fast 96-108 BPM, Chinese courtly folk idiom, warm and lively, instrumental only.
03-方外观静候: Still, reverent waiting outside a small prayer hall at dusk. Solo xiao flute breathing long pentatonic phrases with big silences, occasional guqin harmonic like a distant bell, almost motionless, quiet dignity of someone standing outside a door. Very slow, under 60 BPM, intimate and restrained, no western instruments, no drums, instrumental only.
04-海晏堂水力钟: A great water clock of twelve bronze zodiac heads, Chinese bells and western gears turning together. Bianzhong bronze chimes mark each hour in a twelve-phrase cycle, guzheng arpeggios flow like water, a faint baroque cello bass line hums underneath, twelve phrases rise and finally resolve together at a single noon chime. Steady ceremonial pace about 84 BPM, pentatonic melody over a western bass, instrumental only.
06-终章此处待绘: Warm but unfinished: assembling paper fragments into a picture with one empty center. Sparse piano single notes and guzheng harmonics trade short phrases, fragments of a gentle theme approach each other but never fully join, the music ends on an open unresolved note, like a blank space waiting to be drawn. Slow 60 BPM, tender, restrained, no triumph, no drums, instrumental only.
